items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: So I always believed that Dick Halligan and myself as arrangers for Blood, Sweat & Tears

ctx.x: And I’m happy. I said — and then if they’re playing a little soft I say, “Look,” I play my horn, I said, “This is what a professional volume is.” I’m not bragging. And I fill up the room. I play soft too. I say, “Look” I start with a buzz [scats]. And I give them a couple of hints that I thought of, no one told me this. Two things to think about. Because I remember playing clarinet or alto, like it’s a little mouthpiece, when I was 14 or 15, so you’re blowing into this mouthpiece and you’re trying to do…

helped me with Blood, Sweat & Tears, everything in my life, who I am. Because I like to bridge to people. It’s not for the pat on the back, “Fred you sound great.” It’s because I care about people. So I always believed that Dick Halligan and myself as arrangers for Blood, Sweat & Tears and the original, not quite a leader, Al Kooper, I think we all care about bridging. And I don’t think every jazz player does care about that. So if you don’t dig it man, you know, whatever. I don’t know. I’m just into, and it’s…
Were your parents supportive of a career in music?
